subject: py_type_inference IS a schema amendment, not an omission — and it needed sign-off, which it got
detail: Confirming explicitly since it was asked. Schema v7 §2.21 DELETES py_type_inference as a relation and folds it into four appended py_expression columns, c33 inferredTypeName / c34 inferredTypeKind / c35 inferenceEvidence / c36 inferenceConfidence. The arbiter proposed it, flagged it as touching the frozen spine, and did not make the change unilaterally; I signed off from the implementation side and recorded the reasoning at 2026-08-21T21:00. It is safe by CONSTRUCTION rather than by inspection: the PK is built from c0-c32 only, so appending cannot move a hash, and svc/PK shifting to c37/c38 is what append-only-hash-last does every time. Spine went 262 to 266, and the schema-document ratchet in the test suite caught the change on the first run after the append, which is exactly what it is for. Emitting today, 26.3% of expressions carry an inferred type.

subject: three IR defects in py_expression, found the day it was first adjudicated
detail: The 0%-adjudicated claim for py_expression was correct and checking it paid immediately. The claim for py_call_site was NOT correct — eight content fields including receiverKind are compared against the ast oracle on every call site, and the four CALL_FIELD disagreements I reported earlier came from that very check. py_expression genuinely had only self-consistency invariants, which cannot catch a systematic error: invert every edgeRole and depth-is-parent-plus-one still holds. Three real defects, none visible to any prior gate. (1) UNPACKING TARGETS WERE READS: in `a, b = 1, 2` ast marks both elements Store, while the parser propagated LOAD to every sub-expression of a target — a rule that is right for `self.x = 1`, which really does read `self`, and wrong for a tuple, whose every leaf is assigned. 1,472 names across 100 files. (2) CHAINED ASSIGNMENT LOST ITS MIDDLE TARGETS: tree-sitter nests `a = b = None` as assignment(left=a, right=assignment(...)), so `b` arrived as a VALUE and was recorded as a read; CPython sees one Assign with both targets Store and is plainly right, since `b` is assigned rather than evaluated. (3) A PARENTHESISED ARGUMENT REPORTED POSITION 0: in `re.compile(pattern, (A|B|C))` the second argument was renumbered from its index inside the parentheses, so argument-to-parameter linking would have bound it to the first parameter. Now clean over 117,911 name contexts, 41,633 argument positions, 18,911 receivers and 4,804 nestings.

subject: how the expression adjudicator avoids the shared-author blind spot
detail: Worth stating because A0's caveat about Gate 2 applies to anything I write. This check does NOT reimplement the parser's rules in Python; it READS annotations CPython computed itself. Name.ctx is the interpreter's own Load/Store/Del. The index in Call.args is the interpreter's own argument order. Parentage and nesting come from the interpreter's own tree. A parallel implementation would share my blind spots; reading the interpreter's answers does not. The join is on the (line, utf-8 byte column) SPAN including the end column, which is what makes it exact — keying on the start alone conflates the outer and inner calls in `super().f()`, which share a start offset. I had to add a getEndColumn accessor for this; the column was already stored and in the PK, just not readable.

subject: four empty columns filled, one confirmed correctly empty
detail: py_binding.targetEntityHash: 0 -> 3,447 of 6,286. Same failure as the type_base twin FK and just as invisible — targetEntityKind was written on every row while the hash stayed empty, so a discriminator saying METHOD had nothing to dereference and an orphan check called it healthy. Built by INVERTING declaringBindingLinkHash, which already existed, rather than re-deriving the association and risking a different answer. The remaining 2,839 all have kind NONE and correctly carry no hash. py_field.pyExpressionLinkHash: 0 -> 369/369, joined on the write target's byte range; this is the pointer that makes §2.10's deletion of py_field_write true rather than merely arguable. py_expression.returnStatementIndex: 0 -> 1,690 rows, the 0-based index of the enclosing return within its method, matching Java c19 — it has to ride on the pending record rather than a field, because the worklist drains after the statement visit has moved on. futureImports: the reader was looking for `import_from_statement` when tree-sitter gives `from __future__ import x` its OWN node type, future_import_statement, so it returned empty for every file in existence. Fixed and verified. Note 0/31 on asyncio is CORRECT — the stdlib genuinely has none, and the one grep hit in inspect.py is inside a docstring.

subject: diff-expr promoted out of scratch and wired into the runner
detail: Agreed it was the highest priority and it is done: moved to src/test/python-gates/ and called from python-extractor-tests.ts, so every fixture run adjudicates the expression tree. It should never have stayed in scratch — it found 1,472 unpacking targets recorded as reads, 57 chained-assignment targets and 4 parenthesised arguments at the wrong position, and NONE was visible to any other check, because every prior py_expression assertion is self-consistent. Invert every edgeRole and depth-is-parent-plus-one still holds. Unwired, all three could regress in silence. Also added to the corpus sweep.

subject: gate2 now reads oracle.classifications, and residue turned out to be load-bearing
detail: Wired importKind, methodKind and typeModifier. The detail that matters for your coverage meter: a tier-1 verdict is only authoritative when `residue` is EMPTY. A decorated method arrives as methodKind=INSTANCE_METHOD with residue='DECORATED:property' — that means 'the decorator puts this outside my tier-1 set', not 'it is an instance method'. Comparing against it made the parser wrong for being MORE specific than the oracle chose to be, and produced 8 false failures on the fixtures before I read the residue field. Whatever computes coverage should count a declined verdict as NOT adjudicated, or the number will overstate. typeModifier is compared by CONTAINMENT rather than equality, since the oracle states only the modifiers it is sure of.

subject: gate2 extended to py_field, py_type_base and py_module
detail: py_field <- oracle.attributeWrites, joined on (ownerClass, attribute, origin) with the attribute name MANGLED first: the parser stores _C__x for self.__x, matching the runtime __dict__ key, while the oracle reports the source spelling. Two oracle origins are skipped rather than compared, because they are not py_field rows at all — a write through a receiver that is not the method's own (`other.attr = x`) is an attribute of a different object, which is why the schema's fieldOrigin has no value for it. py_type_base <- structure.classes[].bases, checking position specifically, since C3 rides on base order and a scrambled position silently changes which inherited method a call reaches; a keyword base is position null on the oracle side and '' on mine, both meaning 'not in the MRO'. py_module <- oracle.module for qualifiedName, hasDunderAll, dunderAllIsStatic, dunderAllNames and emissionRegime. py_method_parameter was already compared as name:paramKind pairs and is unchanged. 18/18 fixtures clean, 248/250 stdlib files clean, the remaining 4 being the known receiverKind oracle defect.

subject: oracle defect #7 — a method of a class nested in a function is reported NESTED_FUNCTION
detail: Surfaced immediately by the new methodKind comparison. scoping_edge_cases.py:70 has `def increment(self)` inside `class Counter` inside `outer_with_nested_class`. The oracle says NESTED_FUNCTION; the parser says INSTANCE_METHOD. CPython settles it: the qualname is outer.<locals>.Counter.increment, inspect.isfunction on the class dict entry is True, and inspect.ismethod(C().increment) is True — it binds through an instance, so it is an instance method that happens to live in a nested class. Same shape as oracle defect #6: a check ordered wrongly, testing 'inside another def' before 'inside a class'. Excluded from comparison rather than matched.

subject: SELF is 81.2% on library code, not 30.9% — and the ceiling claim is wrong for a structural reason
detail: The 30.9% predates the module-naming fix; re-measuring the same 18 packages gives 59.1%. But the more important correction is WHY it is not ~100%, because it changes what to work on. Diagnosed on ctypes, which reads worst at 7.9%: 1,303 of its 1,303 unresolved SELF calls are assertEqual/assertRaises on unittest.TestCase subclasses inside ctypes/test/, and the callee name is declared NOWHERE in the corpus — 0/1303 — because unittest is outside the analysis root when rootDir is ctypes. The remaining 487 are real and worth chasing (get_finalized_command, _nametowidget, set_undefined_options — cross-module inheritance within a package), but SELF is no longer the biggest lever. Recommendation for the acceptance corpus: either analyse the whole stdlib as ONE root so unittest is present, or exclude bundled tests. Measuring a package whose test suite subclasses a class outside the root will keep producing numbers that describe the harness rather than the parser.

subject: where resolution actually stands on library code, and the honest ranking
detail: 220 stdlib library files, tests excluded, edge-based (concrete hash, not kind): SELF 81.2%, CLS 77.4%, SUPER 58.1%, NONE 36.3%, NAME 12.6%, CALL_RESULT 7.6%, ATTRIBUTE 2.5%, LITERAL/SUBSCRIPT 0%. So the biggest remaining lever is local-variable typing at ~4,364 sites, not SELF and not py_field.

subject: yes — self-inheritance links with real hashes, and it breaks only where the BASE fails
detail: Answered empirically with a controlled project rather than by reading code. src/test-data/python/inheritance-sample is a two-package project where every target is in-project: framework/ declares TestCase in case.py and RE-EXPORTS it from __init__.py, app/ subclasses it through that re-export. Before the fixes below, `self.assert_equal()` inside the subclass was UNRESOLVED while `self.check_total()` on a locally-declared method resolved fine — which is the whole answer: inherited self-dispatch is a real hash link through py_type_base -> py_type -> py_method along the C3 MRO, and it produces nothing when the base row is unresolved. Every SELF failure I have chased traces back to a base, never to the self-dispatch itself.

subject: package discovery, modelled on the Java parser's registry — three fixes
detail: The human's read was right: this is a discovery/search-path problem, not a resolution problem. Python resolves `import framework` against sys.path, so the name is relative to wherever the package ROOT sits, while a module's qualified name here depends on where analysis started — rooting at a directory that is itself a package makes every module carry that package's name, so `framework` is registered as `sample.framework` and an exact match fails. Three fixes. (1) MODULE SUFFIX INDEX: every module is registered under every dotted suffix of its qualified name, collisions refusing rather than guessing, mirroring what already worked for types. `framework` finds `sample.framework`; if two packages both contain `utils`, the bare name refuses while `framework.utils` resolves. (2) RE-EXPORT CHAINING: a package __init__ saying `from .runner import Runner` does not DECLARE Runner, so `from framework import Runner` resolved to a module and stopped. The walk now follows the chain, bounded at 8 hops and refusing on a cycle. This is how most packages present a public API, and it is the same shape as unittest.TestCase. (3) LOCAL-VARIABLE TYPING: `runner = Runner()` then `runner.run()`. Three grounds — a constructor, a factory's return annotation, a self-method's return annotation — plus parameter annotations for `def run(self, case: TestCase)`. A name assigned two DIFFERENT types maps to null and stays unresolved; that refusal is the point, since a variable reused for two purposes has no single callee.

subject: controlled project 50% -> 95%, and it held at scale rather than overfitting
detail: inheritance-sample went 10/20 to 19/20 edges. The one remaining is self.failures.append() reported BUILTIN, which is correct — the attribute is assigned []. The check that matters is whether it generalised: on 220 stdlib LIBRARY files (bundled tests excluded, since those subclass unittest which is outside the root), total edges 27.5% -> 29.2%, with SELF 81.2% -> 87.1%, NAME 12.6% -> 15.4%, ATTRIBUTE 2.5% -> 3.1%. Smaller than the sample's jump, which is the honest result and the expected one: the sample is fully annotated and self-contained, the stdlib annotates 0.1% of parameters. Nothing regressed — 18/18 fixtures clean on all three gates, 198/200 stdlib files clean, output byte-identical. The original linkage-sample went 36 to 39 of 49 edges.

note: ORACLE DEFECT REGISTER — starting it here as asked, and you are right that you should not be learning about these from the margins of a status report. Outstanding, all adjudicated against CPython at runtime, none matched by the parser. (1) receiverKind on a @staticmethod: configparser.py:553,555 `match.group(1)` inside LegacyInterpolation._interpolation_replace reported SELF. Verified isinstance(LegacyInterpolation.__dict__['_interpolation_replace'], staticmethod) is True, so the first parameter is an ordinary argument and there is no receiver. Parser says NAME. (2) receiverKind on a module-level function: copyreg.py:101,107 `cls.__new__(cls, *args)` inside __newobj__ reported CLS. Verified copyreg.__newobj__.__qualname__ == '__newobj__', so it is module-level and `cls` is just a parameter name. Parser says NAME. Both look like receiver detection keyed on the first parameter's name or position without checking staticmethod-ness or class membership. (3) methodKind for a method of a class nested in a function: scoping_edge_cases.py:70. Reported NESTED_FUNCTION; CPython gives qualname outer.<locals>.Counter.increment and inspect.ismethod(C().increment) is True. Check ordered wrongly — 'inside another def' tested before 'inside a class'. (4) structure.functions omits LAMBDAS entirely: ast.py has 19 by ast.walk, the dump lists 0. Not a defect if intentional, but it made every lambda py_method row read as spurious in my Gate 2 until I excluded them; worth stating in the contract either way. Numbers #6/#7 were my informal labels and I am dropping them — this register is the list.

IR GAP, filed not papered over, and it is the one the human just named: the parser owes correct HOPS even where it cannot build chains. An assignment emits its TARGET and its VALUE as two unrelated depth-0 roots — `node = Node('a')` gives a NAME_REFERENCE with edgeRole ASSIGNMENT_TARGET and a CALL with edgeRole ASSIGNMENT_VALUE, both with parentExpressionHash empty. NOTHING in the emitted IR relates them, so an engine asking 'what flows into this binding' must guess from (scope, line), which breaks on `a = f(); b = g()` and on a value continued to the next line. I hit exactly this in my own resolver and had to add a side table. bindingLinkHash cannot carry it: §2.15 c26 is 'when this node reads or writes a bound name', and in `x = y` it already means y's binding on the value side.
